title: Squared Gaussian quantiles toward the midpoint
statement: Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<a<1$, $0<b<1$, $a\le b$, and $a+b\le1$. Then $Q(b)^2\le Q(a)^2$.
replaced: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and put $Q=\Phi^{-1}$ and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for $0<p<1$. If $a,b\in(0,1)$, $a\le b$, and $a+b\le1$, then $Q(b)^2\le Q(a)^2$.
